advances: Ordinary fixed-cap variation at an interior mark, with a necessary contact condition at local minima.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Let $E(P)$ be the union of the exposed faces $F_K(n)$ with unit normals $n$ satisfying $n\cdot P=h_K(n)$. It is compact as the projection of the closed set of pairs $(n,x)$ satisfying $n\cdot x=n\cdot P=h_K(n)$ in $\mathbb S^{d-1}\times K$. Each such face contains $P$ and is convex, so every other plane has the same strict sign on it as at $P$. Compactness gives an open neighborhood $U$ of $E(P)$ where all these strict signs hold, and we write $J=\{j\ne i:u_j\cdot P>0\}$.

Put $P_\varepsilon=(1+\varepsilon)P$ and $L_\varepsilon=\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{P_\varepsilon\})$. The point $P_\varepsilon$ lies outside $K$ because $P$ is the radial endpoint from $0$. The whole added region eventually lies in $U$. Otherwise take $x_k\in L_{\varepsilon_k}\setminus(K\cup U)$ with $\varepsilon_k\downarrow0$, converging after a subsequence to $x\in K\setminus U$ by the containment $L_\varepsilon\subseteq K+\varepsilon\lVert P\rVert B_d$. Unit normals $n_k$ strictly separating $x_k$ from $K$ satisfy $n_k\cdot P_{\varepsilon_k}>h_K(n_k)$, by the support formula of the hull. Passing to a convergent subsequence of normals puts both $P$ and $x$ in the same exposed face, a contradiction. The added region has positive volumes $D_+,D_-$ on each side of $\Pi_i$: a ball at $0$ contained in $K$ and the exterior apex span cones on both sides entering any sufficiently small ball at the apex disjoint from $K$. Thus the total added volume $D=D_++D_-$ is positive and tends to zero by the outer containment. The fill adds $D$ to the caps in $J$, $D_+$ to cap $i$, and zero to the others.

To find a removable cap with signs $J$ and the positive $i$ side, take a nonzero $n$ in the closed normal cone $N_K(P)=\{w:w\cdot(x-P)\le0\ \forall x\in K\}$. Neither $u_i$ nor $-u_i$ lies in this cone because $P\in\Pi_i$ and $0$ is interior. Hence $n$ is not parallel to $u_i$. The ray $n+t u_i$ has a finite last point $n_*$ in the cone: if the parameters were unbounded, division by $t$ and closure would put $u_i$ in the cone. The vector $n_*$ is nonzero. For each $\delta>0$ the functional $\ell_\delta=n_*+\delta u_i$ is outside the cone and $h_K(\ell_\delta)>\ell_\delta\cdot P=n_*\cdot P$. For every $x\in F_K(\ell_\delta)$, the inequality $n_*\cdot x\le n_*\cdot P$ then gives $\delta u_i\cdot x>0$. These faces approach $F_K(n_*)\subseteq E(P)$ in the sense that every cluster point as $\delta\downarrow0$ lies in that face. This follows from compactness and continuity of support values. Fix small $\delta$ so its entire exposed face is in $U$.

Write $\ell=\ell_\delta$ and $h=h_K(\ell)>0$. Choose a fixed depth $\eta_0>0$ so the closed cap of $K$ at threshold $h-\eta_0$ has the desired strict signs on every plane. This is possible because such caps approach the selected face, which is compactly contained in that signature region. Also choose $\eta_0<\min(h/2,h-\ell\cdot P)$. For small $\varepsilon$, $\ell\cdot P_\varepsilon<h-\eta_0$. Thus $L_\varepsilon$ has support $h$ in this direction, and its cap at depth $\eta_0$ has the same strict signs by compactness and Hausdorff convergence. Its volume is at least the positive volume of the fixed old cap. Continuity of cap volume in depth yields a depth $\eta(\varepsilon)\in(0,\eta_0)$ at which the actual $L_\varepsilon$ cap has volume $D$. Any fixed positive depth eventually gives more than $D$ because it contains a positive-volume old cap, so $\eta(\varepsilon)\to0$.

Shave that cap by setting $K_\varepsilon=L_\varepsilon\cap\{\ell\cdot x\le h-\eta(\varepsilon)\}$. It restores total volume, cancels the fill on all caps in $J$, and changes the selected cap by $D_+-D=-D_-<0$. The shave misses every central plane, and the fill misses every unselected plane. On the selected plane the filled section is $\operatorname{conv}((K\cap\Pi_i)\cup\{P_\varepsilon\})$, since any convex combination with the apex in $\Pi_i$ has to use an old point in $\Pi_i$ unless it is just the apex. The new exterior point increases relative volume strictly by the exterior-point and interior-ball argument in $\Pi_i$. The inclusions
$$
(1-\eta(\varepsilon)/h)K\subseteq K_\varepsilon
\subseteq K+\varepsilon\lVert P\rVert B_d
$$
show that the mark stays interior and give Hausdorff convergence.

If $K$ is strictly convex, its exposed faces are singletons. The finitely many proper subspaces $\Pi_i\cap\Pi_j$ do not cover $\Pi_i$, so a ray in $\Pi_i$ avoiding them ends at a suitable $P$. For at least two cuts, decreasing $1/\sigma_i$ while all other inverse section measures stay fixed strictly decreases $\lambda_i$ and strictly increases the others. In the fixed-volume upper-constraint class the variation is feasible by coordinatewise monotonicity. Thus, with at least two cuts, a localized star contradicts local minimality, including for any initially minimizing index of the minimum objective. An exposed face through a point outside another cut plane that meets that plane is nontrivial. In the plane the intersection of distinct central lines is only the interior mark, so both chord endpoints satisfy the avoidance requirement.

statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Let $\Pi_j=\{x:u_j\cdot x=0\}$ be finitely many pairwise distinct unoriented hyperplanes with $u_j\ne0$. Define $q_j(K)=|K\cap\{u_j\cdot x\ge0\}|$ and $\sigma_j(K)=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap\Pi_j)/\lVert u_j\rVert$. Fix $i$ and suppose there is $P\in\partial K\cap\Pi_i$ whose union of all exposed faces containing $P$ misses every $\Pi_j$ with $j\ne i$. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is a convex body $K_\varepsilon$ containing $0$ in its interior and tending to $K$ in Hausdorff distance, with
$$
|K_\varepsilon|=|K|,\quad q_i(K_\varepsilon)<q_i(K),\quad
\sigma_i(K_\varepsilon)>\sigma_i(K),
$$
with every other cap volume unchanged and every other central section unchanged as a set. If there are at least two planes, $\lambda_i=(1/\sigma_i)/\sum_j(1/\sigma_j)$ decreases strictly and every other weight increases. The hypothesis on $P$ always holds if $K$ is strictly convex.

Consequently, if there are at least two planes, in a fixed-volume class containing only constraints of the form $F(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\le c$ with coordinatewise nondecreasing $F$, among bodies with $0$ interior, at a local minimum of $\lambda_i$ every $P\in\partial K\cap\Pi_i$ outside the other planes must belong to a nontrivial exposed face meeting another plane. At a local minimum of $\min_j\lambda_j$ this holds for every index attaining the minimum. In the plane this applies to both endpoints of each relevant chord.
title: A localized contact star permits exact central cap and section variation
